LOOK: DSWD personnel and volunteers prepare family food packs at the DSWD National Resource Operations Center warehouse in Pasay City on Tuesday, Nov. 4. 

These packs will be distributed to families affected by Typhoon Tino, which battered parts of Eastern and Central Visayas, including Leyte, Southern Leyte, Cebu, and Northern Negros, as well as Dinagat Islands and Siargao. 

The typhoon brought destructive winds and torrential rains, causing flooding and power outages. 

📸: Mark Balmores/MB

🚨🌪️ TYPHOON KALMAEGI BATTERS CENTRAL PHILIPPINES — MASS EVACUATIONS, RESCUE OPERATIONS UNDERWAY 🇵🇭

MANILA, Nov 4 (Reuters) — Typhoon Kalmaegi (Tino) slammed into the central Philippines with winds up to 205 kph, unleashing torrential rains, storm surges, and massive flooding across the Visayas. One person has died, and tens of thousands have been evacuated from vulnerable coastal and low-lying areas.

🔹Videos from Talisay and Cebu City show submerged homes and vehicles, while residents in Liloan, Bacayan, and Villa Lara are pleading for urgent rescue on social media 

 🔹Authorities warn of 3-meter-high storm surges and have canceled over 160 flights. Kalmaegi is expected to exit into the South China Sea by Wednesday, possibly making a second landfall in Vietnam.

💔 The Philippines, hit by an average of 20 storms yearly, continues to face overlapping natural disasters.

-Reuters
